newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan government sells 30,000 shares in China Steel.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan government sells 30,000 shares in China Steel.

text.p: Taiwan's economics ministry on Tuesday auctioned off some 30,000 shares in China Steel, Taiwan's largest steel firm, as part of its plan to sell 182.19 million shares in the concern.
The latest small sale, worth 969,000 Taiwan dollars ($33,700), was to a single bidder, an official from the Taiwan Stock Exchange said by telephone. The sale price was T$32.3 per share.
China Steel ended trading on Tuesday at T$31.8, up 30 cents.

The government began its sale of China Steel shares on Monday, auctioneering off some 92.79 million shares for T$2.89 billion, and plans to complete the operation in four days. Its stake in China Steel will be reduced to 39.2 from 42.1 percent.
The sell-off is part of a five-year process to sell the government's entire China Steel stake, officials have said.
Taiwan's finance ministry last week auctioned some 418 million shares in Chiao Tung Bank -- a sell-off that reduced state's stake in the bank to 60.03 percent from 88.83 percent.
Taiwan's government said in January it planned to release some 800 million state-owned shares worth some T$100 billion in fiscal 1997/98 (July/June).

Taiwan said in July that the government's privatisation scheme would accelerate from the middle of 1998, outlining plans to release state-owned shares worth T$450 billion over the next three fiscal years. ($ = 28.72 Taiwan Dollars)
